items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: when I first started I didn’t have a vehicle, she was chauffeuring me to every performance and rehearsal

ctx.x: Oh yes well because I had — well I didn’t actually just switch, you know. I didn’t say I’m playing guitar today and tomorrow I’m playing bass. It was gradual. So I just kind of played bass on the side. I also played, when I was in high school, a year I did bassoon, I played baritone horn in the marching band. I did a lot of different instruments, and bass was just one of them. And so it was really gradual. And it wasn’t until like maybe my senior year of high school that I actually decided that I was going to…

bass. Because up until that point I was doing so much guitar work, and I hadn’t had any formal lessons on the bass, you know I’d just basically taught myself, so like my technique wasn’t really great or anything. But I started finding more and more opportunities. I was playing, I was enjoying it more, and I really liked the style of music that I was able to improvise and put in my own voice to the music. And so it was just gradual. And my mother’s been always very supportive of whatever instrument that I wanted…
How does she feel about you being in these New York City nightclubs?
